questions.evidence:
On her way home, Nora buys a notebook for sixty dollars and a pen for twenty. She pays with a hundred-dollar note. The cashier gives her ten dollars in change and puts the receipt inside the notebook before serving the next customer.

Nora notices the problem outside the shop. She checks the prices on the receipt before returning to the counter. It lists one notebook, one pen, and a ten-dollar gift bag. She did not buy or receive a gift bag.

The cashier checks the items and apologizes. The bag was left on the screen from a canceled purchase. He removes that charge and returns ten dollars to Nora. She thanks him for explaining what happened.

At home, Nora keeps the receipt for a week because the notebook has a return policy for printing problems. The store accepts such returns within seven days, but only if the customer shows proof of purchase.

Nora notices the problem outside the shop. She checks the prices on the receipt before returning to the counter. It lists one notebook, one pen, and a ten-dollar gift bag. She did not buy or receive a gift bag.

The cashier checks the items and apologizes. The bag was left on the screen from a canceled purchase. He removes that charge and returns ten dollars to Nora. She thanks him for explaining what happened.

At home, Nora keeps the receipt for a week because the notebook has a return policy for printing problems. The store accepts such returns within seven days, but only if the customer shows proof of purchase.
